item.title: New online registry helps tradespeople work across Canada
item.description:
New online registry helps tradespeople work across Canada jenniferdhogan Wed, 09/16/2026 - 09:20

The Government of Prince Edward Island has launched an online registry of skilled tradespeople that makes it easier for employers to verify credentials and supports labour mobility across the country.

The online registry will help employers, contractors and homeowners verify whether a person holds a Prince Edward Island Certificate of Qualification or Red Seal endorsement and the trade in which they are certified. Searches can be done using identifying information such as a name and certification number. 

"Skilled tradespeople are essential to building and maintaining the homes, infrastructure, and businesses our communities rely on. This registry makes it easier for certified tradespeople and apprentices to demonstrate their qualifications, have their credentials recognized, and pursue employment opportunities both in PEI and across Canada. At the same time, it gives employers a more efficient way to verify credentials, helping connect qualified workers with jobs when and where they are needed most."

- Minister of Workforce and Advanced Learning Jenn Redmond

While apprenticeship and trade certification credentials have traditionally been verified through provincial apprenticeship offices, the self-service tool provides immediate access to credential information, reducing administrative steps for workers, employers, and industry partners. 

The registry fulfills a commitment in the department's mandate letter by modernizing access to apprenticeship and certification information while supporting the province’s goal of strengthening labour mobility and workforce development across Canada.

 

Media contact:
April Gallant

item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running. I know the efforts and economic impacts of the pipeline have already begun to take shape in the community and will be felt for years to come. ”

 

Charlotte Digness
Media and Communications Coordinator
Cabinet Communications and Protocol
Government of the Northwest Territories
